intended_object: Given a topological space X, a family of types T x for x ∈ X, and a local predicate P on dependent functions, this is the sheaf of types on X whose sections over an open U are the dependent functions f : ∀ x ∈ U, T x that satisfy P. It is a subsheaf of the sheaf of all such functions. This comes from the docstring and the module.
explanation:
The definition bundles two things into a `Sheaf (Type _) X`:
- the presheaf `subpresheafToTypes P.toPrelocalPredicate`, which sends U to `{f : ∀ x : U, T x // P.pred f}`, with restriction given by restricting functions;
- the proof `subpresheafToTypes.isSheaf`, which shows the sheaf condition by gluing in the sheaf of all functions and then using the locality of P.

This is exactly the standard construction of the sheaf of functions satisfying a local condition, such as continuous or locally constant functions, used for example to build the étale-space and structure sheaves. Its setting is fully general: any topological space, any family of types and any local predicate. I found no other Mathlib declaration that duplicates it.
